passage:
There is an old radio in Mr. Wang's noodle shop. It sits near the door and plays songs from many years ago.
One day, a young customer asked, "Why don't you use a newer speaker This radio sounds strange."
Mr. Wang smiled. "That strange sound is part of the shop."
He explained that the radio belonged to his mother. When the shop first opened, she used it to listen to music while making noodles. After she passed away, Mr. Wang kept the radio on the same shelf.
The young customer did not say much. The next week, he came back with his grandfather. They ordered noodles and sat near the radio. His grandfather listened quietly for a while and then began to sing along.
After they left, the young customer said, "Now I understand. Some old things do not sound perfect, but they carry voices that new things cannot."
